rentalYield.title: Rental Yield Calculator
rentalYield.subtitle: Calculate gross, net and cash-on-cash yields for officetels, retail units and homes, plus monthly cash flow, break-even rent and the price or rent needed to hit a target yield.

typeHint.house: Acquisition tax 1–3% (8–12% surcharge for multiple homes in regulated areas), brokerage cap 0.4–0.7%.
typeHint.officetel: Acquisition tax 4.6% (incl. rural and education taxes), brokerage cap 0.5% for residential-grade officetels (0.9% otherwise).
typeHint.store: Acquisition tax 4.6% (incl. rural and education taxes), brokerage cap 0.9%.

target.title: Solve for a target yield
target.desc: See the rent needed to reach your target net yield, or the highest price you can pay at the current rent.
target.priceHint: {read} KRW · {diff} KRW vs current price (costs recalculated)
target.none: Not reachable — the target must be above 0%, vacancy below 100%, and rent income must exceed operating costs.

sens.title: Rate & vacancy sensitivity
sens.desc: Monthly cash flow (top) and cash-on-cash yield (bottom) when the rate moves ±1%p or vacancy rises.
sens.descNoLoan: No loan, so the rate has no effect. Compare cash flow (top) and yield (bottom) by vacancy.
sens.caption: Monthly cash flow and cash-on-cash yield by interest rate and vacancy
sens.note: The blue cell matches your current inputs. With a variable-rate loan, check that the +1%p row still works.

rentalYield.disclaimer: This is a pre-tax estimate based on your inputs, not investment advice. Actual taxes, loan terms and fees vary by contract and region.

formula.title: Three yields, three meanings
items: Gross yield = annual rent ÷ (price − deposit). Common in sales ads; it ignores taxes, fees, vacancy and running costs, so it looks higher than reality.
Net yield = net operating income ÷ (price + acquisition costs − deposit). NOI is rent after vacancy minus owner-paid fees, repairs and holding taxes. Use this to compare properties.
Cash-on-cash yield = (NOI − first-year interest) ÷ your cash. Your cash is what you put in after the deposit and loan. A loan only boosts this when its rate is below the net yield.
Monthly cash flow = NOI ÷ 12 − monthly loan payment. With an amortizing loan, principal leaves your pocket too, so cash flow can be negative even with a positive yield.
Break-even rent is the rent at which operating costs and first-year interest leave zero profit, with vacancy included.

costs.title: Acquisition and holding costs
items: Acquisition tax: officetels and retail pay 4% plus 0.2% rural tax and 0.4% education tax = 4.6% (Local Tax Act Art. 11(1)7(b), Art. 151). Homes pay 1–3%, with 8–12% surcharges for multiple homes in regulated areas.
Brokerage: the buyer's legal cap plus 10% VAT. Homes 0.4–0.7% by bracket, residential-grade officetels 0.5%, retail and other officetels up to 0.9%.
Registration costs: an estimate of the housing bond discount (assessed value assumed at 70% of price), the buyer's half of stamp duty and a 600,000 KRW scrivener fee.
Holding taxes: property and comprehensive real estate taxes depend on assessed values and the number of homes, so enter your own figure. Use the holding tax calculator first.
Vacancy: the share of the year the unit sits empty. One month ≈ 8.3%. Include re-letting brokerage and redecorating in repairs for a realistic figure.

tax.title: Rental income tax (reference only — not calculated)
items: Reference: rent from a single home is tax-exempt, except homes with a standard value over 1.2B KRW and homes abroad (Income Tax Act Art. 12(2)(b)).

Reference: if total housing rent is 20M KRW or less a year, you can choose 14% separate taxation. It deducts 50% expenses (60% for registered rentals) and 2M KRW (4M registered) if other income is 20M KRW or less (Art. 14(3)7, Art. 64-2).

Reference: owners of 3+ homes with total deposits over 300M KRW are also taxed on deemed rent from deposits. Small homes (≤40㎡ and ≤200M KRW standard value) are excluded from the count through 2026 (Art. 25(1)).
Reference: commercial rent is subject to 10% VAT that the landlord collects and files; housing rent is VAT-exempt (VAT Act Art. 26(1)12).
Reference: residential officetels taxed as homes count toward the number of homes for acquisition tax surcharges (Local Tax Act Art. 13-3(4)). Confirm exact taxes with the NTS or a tax professional.

check.title: Before you buy
items: Check whether an advertised '7% yield' is gross or leveraged. The same property can differ by 1–3%p depending on the formula.
If the loan rate is above the net yield, borrowing more lowers your cash-on-cash yield (negative leverage). Use the sensitivity table to test +1%p.
Guaranteed-return periods on new officetels and retail units end, and rent reverts to market. Check real nearby rents and vacancy.
When trading deposit for rent, compare with the jeonse–wolse conversion rate. The legal cap is in the rent converter.
Selling adds capital gains tax and brokerage again. Rental yield covers holding only; price gains or losses are separate.
